simple.meaning: סָחַר (çâchar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to travel round (specifically as a pedlar); intensively, to palpitate.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 21 times in Genesis, 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, Proverbs, and 3 more, beginning at Genesis 23:16. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, kingship, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סָחַר (H5503) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: סָחַר (çâchar) / H5503 is traced through Genesis 23:16, Genesis 34:10, Genesis 34:21, Genesis 37:28 with source-language evidence and verse context.
